thread:
ashley.support: FYI a customer (acct: acme-retail) opened a high-priority ticket — lots of 5xxs + timeouts hitting their checkout flow hitting our hosted inference gateway. They're seeing failed checkout events and billing anomalies. Escalating to war room.

maria.sre: on it. can you paste sample request ids?

ashley.support: pasted in the ticket: reqs: `rq_2026031701`, `rq_2026031702`, `rq_2026031709`. Customer says spike started ~09:12 UTC and is ongoing. They've attached traces that show gateway 502/504. :exclamation:

incident-bot: New incident created: INC-2026-0317-67 — assigned to oncall.

maria.sre: seeing elevated 502s from hosted-gateway in eu-west during that window. p50 latency ok but p95+p99 huge. moving to war-room channel. @kevin.backend @devon.platform please join.

kevin.backend: joining. i pulled trace for `rq_2026031701` — upstream inference returned `context deadline exceeded` then gateway returned 504. stack sample: ```
2026-03-17T09:12:45Z inference-runtime: kv-cache miss, invoking model:v3.2.1
2026-03-17T09:12:49Z model-worker: seq=1 run failed: rpc timeout
2026-03-17T09:12:49Z gateway: returning 504 to client req=rq_2026031701
```

kevin.backend: recent canary deploy of model runtime `v3.2.1` went live at 09:00 UTC. canary was 20% traffic to hosted. might correlate.

devon.platform: infra metrics show a burst of long tail GPU scheduling latencies + node churn in eu-west around 09:10-09:20. autoscaler triggered several new pods but some failed healthchecks (OOMKill).

maria.sre: hypothesis: model runtime canary + memory/regression => longer model startup/oom => requests queueing at gateway => timeouts. mitigation options: 1) remove canary (route traffic to stable), 2) temporarily increase gateway timeouts and enable fallback to smaller model, 3) scale dedicated pool for acme-retail, 4) circuit-break on long-running requests.

oliver.prod: customer SLA is 99.9% for checkout path. We should prioritize quick rollback or a routing fix. Can we route acme-retail traffic to eu-fallback region while we fix?

devon.platform: we can apply a routing override per-customer in the router. quick plan: (a) enable per-customer routing rule to route acme-retail to eu-fallback (b) rollback canary traffic to stable runtime (c) increase keepalive and reduce max-inflight per-gateway to avoid head-of-line.

kevin.backend: rolling back canary now — `deploy-bot` should show progress.

deploy-bot: rollback started for runtime canary v3.2.1 -> v3.1.8. 12/15 canary hosts replaced. expected full rollback ~2m.

maria.sre: while rollback proceeds, enable model-fallback: add prefix rule to use model v2-compact for requests > 1.5s to avoid cost but reduce tail. `PATCH /routing/overrides`: ```json
{"customer":"acme-retail","fallback_model":"v2-compact","threshold_ms":1500}```

kevin.backend: adding a temporary circuit-break at gateway for requests > 10s to fail fast with 503 and fallthrough to retry logic. Will add logging to capture worker PID + mem usage for failing runs.

ashley.support: I've told the customer we're on it, routing changes + rollback in progress. asked for their preferred maintenance window if needed; they said now, do whatever is needed.

maria.sre: update: rollback finished at 09:16 UTC. canary is out. early signals: p99 latency dropping but still some residual 504s.

devon.platform: routing override applied for acme-retail -> eu-fallback at 09:18 UTC. we also bumped node pool by +2 and adjusted autoscaler headroom. healthchecks stabilized.

kevin.backend: logs show that the problematic model had a regression in kv-cache cold-path causing OOM on certain payload shapes. file: `runtime/handlers/cache.go` line ~247 — suspicious allocation pattern. added TODO to revert that change in next patch.

maria.sre: containment done. moving to postmortem follow-up channel after triage. immediate action items: 
- AC1: create rollback playbook for canary -> owner kevin.backend
- AC2: add per-customer emergency routing toggle in console (engineer: devon.platform)
- AC3: add p95/p99 model-startup health metric and alert (owner: maria.sre)
- AC4: add automated fallback to smaller quantized model after 1.2s (owner: kevin.backend)
- AC5: update runbook for billing reconciliation with support (owner: ashley.support)

ashley.support: noting AC5, I'll kick off a customer billing check and request list of failed order ids.

kevin.backend: created GH issue: `infra#4128` - rollback-playbook + instrumentation. will PR later today.

devon.platform: feature request: make the per-customer routing toggle available via API and console. adding to backlog and will scope MVP in the next sprint.

maria.sre: retrospective notes: canary % should be limited with stronger preflight (kv-cache warmup), add canary-specific healthchecks for memory growth, and add automated rollback if p99 breach > 5x baseline within 5m.

oliver.prod: agree — need tighter SLA guardrails on model/runtime onboard. also let's prep a short customer comms draft once billing reconciliation is done.

ashley.support: customer update sent at 09:40 UTC: "We've routed your traffic to a stable fallback and rolled back the recent runtime canary. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with billing reconciliation." they responded :thumbsup:.

maria.sre: logging summary saved to incident ticket INC-2026-0317-67. moving to postmortem writeup.

kevin.backend: quick repro steps I recorded: 
1) use payload shape with ~12k tokens prefix + long embedding vector request
2) hit `/v1/generate-checkout` with concurrency 10
3) observe memory spike in model-worker within 30s -> OOM or long GC

maria.sre: added action owners to Triage board. will schedule postmortem doc for tomorrow 11:00 UTC. please add notes before EOD.

ashley.support: closing war-room thread, handing off to postmortem channel. thanks all. :pray:
